summary: Source-anchored research for Equality-Sort-Range index ordering. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: ESR is a workload guideline: put all equality predicates first, in any relative order. Put sort fields before range fields when avoiding an in-memory sort matters, or use ERS when a range predicate is very selective and reducing scan work matters more. (high confidence)

A compound index orders keys by the declared field sequence. MongoDB can use an index to obtain a requested sort on a non-prefix subset of keys when the query has equality conditions on all prefix keys that precede the sort keys. Placing a range filter before the sort fields in the index generally means MongoDB cannot avoid an in-memory sort; the explain plan then shows a SORT stage. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md
The ESR classification treats operators such as $ne, $nin, and $regex as range predicates rather than exact-match equality predicates. (high confidence)

Compare ESR and ERS on representative data with explain('executionStats') and index hints. A SORT stage identifies an in-memory ordering step; compare totalKeysExamined and totalDocsExamined with nReturned to decide whether avoiding the sort outweighs scanning more index keys. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md

For one query with equality predicates on several fields, the equality keys need not be ordered by selectivity. Their order still controls which leading index prefixes can support other query patterns, so choose an order that preserves useful prefixes. (high confidence)

With $in combined with sort, the current MongoDB guide treats lists with fewer than 201 values as equality probes that can be merged in sort order; lists of 201 or more act like a range and prevent later index keys from supplying the sort. The guide warns that this cutoff can change across versions. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

MongoDB stores compound-index keys in the declared field sequence. The leftmost prefixes determine which query shapes the index supports, and sort use depends on equality constraints on preceding keys. (high confidence)

For a query with equality predicates, a sort, and a range, the baseline ESR order puts equality keys first, sort keys next, and range keys last. Equality keys can appear in any order relative to each other, but all equality keys must precede any sort or range fields. An index supports a sort on a subset of its keys only when the query has equality conditions on all prefix keys that precede the sort keys. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md
